To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the percentage of endplates innervated by large diameter axons and motor nerve terminals in the epitrochleoanconoeus (ETA) muscle of hSOD1G85R mice is significantly decreased as mice become symptomatic.

(1) the number of large-diameter motor axons and the percentage of endplates innervated by terminals decrease as SOD1-G93A mice become symptomatic; (2) most remaining terminals retain their ability to respond to nerve impulses, although with functional changes; (3) the percentage of innervated endplates correlates with the number of axons in the nerve; (4) the number of innervated terminals is not reduced until late in the disease course; (

1) motor terminal function is altered in hSOD1G85R mice; 2) the number and diameter of axons innervating ETA are reduced in hSOD-G85R mice; and 3) motor terminals are denervated as hSOD1 G85R mice become symptomatic
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms that lead to the degeneration of the motor neurons and their axonal projections, which is the cause of amyotrophic lateral scleroses.
understanding the mechanisms underlying denervation in fALS, and the functional changes that occur in motor terminals in presymptomatically and symptomatically affected muscles.
the mechanisms underlying motor neuron degeneration and the resulting denervation and muscle atrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the denervation of fast limb muscles in hSOD1 mice is not due to the degeneration of motor terminals, but rather to the degeneration or dysfunction of axons, which is a result of a failure of axonal transport and/or an increased vulnerability of axons to stressors.

the denervation of ETA motor terminals in presymptomatically and symptomatic SOD1 mice is a consequence of a loss of axonal caliber and motor terminal dysfunction, which are not necessarily linked to motor neuron death.
the denervation process in fast muscles of SOD1-G86R mice is a gradual process, which begins before symptoms are evident and is not associated with motor terminal dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the innervation of fast limb muscles becomes compromised in SOD1 mutant mice, but that the extent of this denervation is not sufficient to cause muscle atrophy or weakness.

motor terminals in fast forelimb muscles of hSOD1 mice are able to respond to stimulation, but that their responses are altered, with changes in the relative contributions of Ca2+ and exo/endocytic processes to synaptic vesicle recycling.
the innervation of ETA muscle in presymptometric SOD1-G8SR mouse is not significantly different from the wild-type, but the innervation of muscle is significantly reduced in symptomatic SOD1 mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in presymptomic mice, there are no obvious changes in the morphology or function of motor terminals innervated by large diameter axons, whereas symptomatic mice have both a reduction in the number of large-diameter axons and a decrease in the proportion of innervated endplates.
the innervation of fast limb muscles remains relatively intact in presymptomtic hSOD1 mice.

motor terminals remain functional in presymptomatically hSOD1G85R mice but with altered responses to nerve stimulation, and that the number of large axons in the nerve is a good correlate of the number of innervating motor terminals.
